title: Honey and Lavender Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Honey replaces the sugar and dried lavender is steeped instead of vanilla.
summary: Our classic custard, sweetened with honey instead of sugar and steeped with dried lavender instead of vanilla. Floral, soft and summery.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Combine the cream, milk and salt in the saucepan, bring slowly to a simmer, then stir in the lavender, cover and remove from the heat for 30 min. Taste and steep up to 15 min more if you want a stronger flavour.

steps.title: Prepare the yolks
steps.text: Whisk the yolks with the honey in the heatproof bowl until smooth; honey blends more easily if it is runny.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Reheat the infused dairy until hot but not simmering, then pour it through the sieve onto the yolks, whisking all the while. Discard the flowers and return the mixture to a clean pan.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir over low heat until the custard thickens and a line drawn on the spatula holds, at 77-80 °C.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cool the custard over the iced water and refrigerate for at least 4 h; an overnight rest improves the flavour and texture.

steps.title: Churn and freeze
steps.text: Churn until thick and freeze until firm, at least 4 h.

tips: Buy culinary lavender; lavender sold for crafts may be treated.
A common mistake is using too much lavender, which tastes soapy. Start with the recipe amount and taste.
A mild honey such as acacia or clover lets the lavender come through.
storage: Freeze in a covered container for up to 2 weeks.
